components.css: :host{--ramp-0:#0a0910;--bg:#0f0e14;--surface:#17151f;--surface-2:#211d2c;--rule:#2a2638;--edge:#6e6789;--ink:#f5f3fa;--muted:#aaa4bf;--violet:#7030e0;--violet-press:#5f24c4;--lav:#a19df0;--good:#5ee0a0;--warn:#f5c04e;--bad:#ff7a90} .ds-card{width:340px;display:grid;gap:6px;padding:18px 16px 8px;border-radius:14px;background:var(--surface);border:1px solid var(--rule);color:var(--ink);font:400 16px/1.5 Archivo,system-ui,sans-serif} .ds-tag{justify-self:start;padding:2px 8px;border-radius:4px;border:1px solid rgba(161,157,240,.4);color:var(--lav);font:600 12px/1.2 Archivo,sans-serif} .ds-venue{margin:4px 0 0;font:800 30px/1.02 "Big Shoulders Display","Archivo Narrow",sans-serif;text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.01em} .ds-when{margin:0;font:600 16px/1.35 Archivo,sans-serif} .ds-links{display:flex;gap:16px} .ds-links a{color:var(--lav);font:600 14.5px Archivo,sans-serif;line-height:40px} .ds-rsvp{display:grid;gap:8px;margin-top:8px;padding-top:14px;border-top:1px solid var(--rule);font:600 14.5px Archivo,sans-serif} .ds-seg{display:grid;grid-auto-flow:column;grid-auto-columns:1fr;border:1px solid var(--edge);border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden} .ds-seg button{min-height:44px;border:0;border-left:1px solid var(--edge);background:transparent;color:var(--muted);font:700 14.5px Archivo,sans-serif} .ds-seg button:first-child{border-left:0} .ds-seg button[aria-pressed=true]{background:var(--violet);color:#fff} .ds-ride{display:grid;margin-top:6px;padding:10px 0;border-top:1px solid var(--rule);color:var(--muted);font:400 13.5px/1.3 Archivo,sans-serif} .ds-ride b{color:var(--ink);font:700 15px/1.3 Archivo,sans-serif;margin-top:2px}

components.css: :host{--ramp-0:#0a0910;--bg:#0f0e14;--surface:#17151f;--surface-2:#211d2c;--rule:#2a2638;--edge:#6e6789;--ink:#f5f3fa;--muted:#aaa4bf;--violet:#7030e0;--violet-press:#5f24c4;--lav:#a19df0;--good:#5ee0a0;--warn:#f5c04e;--bad:#ff7a90} .ds-tabs{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(5,1fr);width:360px;background:var(--bg);border-top:1px solid var(--rule)}.ds-tabs a{position:relative;padding:20px 0 10px;text-align:center;font:600 12px "Archivo", system-ui, sans-serif;color:var(--muted);cursor:pointer}.ds-tabs a:hover{color:var(--ink)}.ds-tabs a[aria-current]{color:var(--lav)}.ds-tabs a[aria-current]::after{content:"";position:absolute;left:50%;bottom:4px;width:4px;height:4px;margin-left:-2px;border-radius:50%;background:var(--lav)}.ds-tabs b{position:absolute;top:3px;left:calc(50% + 4px);min-width:18px;height:18px;border-radius:9px;background:var(--bad);color:var(--ramp-0);font:700 11px/18px "JetBrains Mono", ui-monospace, monospace}

narrative.overview:
Squadup should feel as easy as the group chat it replaces. Open a squad and the first thing you see is one plan card: where, when, are you coming, and how you're getting there. Below it is a short "Needs you" list, then a two-line summary of the squad. Everything else is one tap away, and anything extra (adding a timetable stop, pinning info, adding a poll option, logging spending, the money breakdown, recent activity) stays folded behind a lavender toggle until someone asks for it.

It replaced the "Departures" look (boarding pass, departure board, split-flap letters, car codes like SQ10). Friends testing it found that look hard to use and confusing, so the metaphor is gone. The brand stays: the logo's violet and lavender on a violet-black night palette, and condensed Big Shoulders signage for the few big moments.

It is dark by design, because it is opened on phones at night, in cars and outside venues.
keyCharacteristics: One plan card on Home; everything else is a ruled list.
Extras are folded: an option appears only when someone taps its toggle.
One violet-black tonal ramp for every neutral, from `ramp-0` (#0a0910) to `ink` (#f5f3fa).
Logo violet fills primary actions and selected segments; lavender marks links, toggles, the active tab, focus and whatever is yours.
Big Shoulders only for the landing headline, screen titles and the venue on the plan card. Archivo for everything you read. JetBrains Mono only for times and money.
No codes, no flipping letters, no ticket shapes.

rules.name: The One Ramp Rule
rules.body: Every neutral comes from the violet-black ramp.

rules.name: The Signal Wash Rule
rules.body: Green, amber and rose appear as text, 1px strokes at 40 to 55% opacity, or a 12% wash. Solid fills are only for the control or alert that resolves the moment (Accept, a ticked task, the outside banner, the error toast, badge counts, the money meter).

rules.name: The Few Signs Rule
rules.body: Big Shoulders appears in three places only: the landing headline, screen titles and the plan-card venue. Section heads, sheet titles, labels and facts are Archivo in sentence case.

rules.name: The Numbers Rule
rules.body: Times and money use JetBrains Mono with tabular numbers. Dates and sentences never do.

rules.name: The Fold Rule
rules.body: A screen shows what most people need right now. Secondary actions and detail (add a stop, pin info, add a poll option, close or delete a poll, rough area, change pickup spot, log spending, money breakdown, recent activity) sit behind a lavender toggle with a plus icon and open in place. A toggle's open state survives live updates.

dos: Do answer "where, when, am I coming, how am I getting there" in the plan card before anything else.
Do fold secondary actions behind a lavender toggle instead of showing every form at once.
Do describe status in plain words ("Aisha is picking you up", "2 free").
Do take every neutral from the ramp and keep violet for fills, lavender for marks.
Do keep touch targets at least 44px and focus visible as a 2px lavender outline.
Do strike through what is done rather than hiding it.
donts: Don't bring back ticket or airport metaphors: no boarding pass, tear lines, departure board, split-flap letters or codes like SQ10 and P01.
Don't set section heads, labels or sheet titles in uppercase Big Shoulders.
Don't show a form that most people won't use on this visit; fold it.
Don't add shadows outside sheets and the toast.
Don't add a light theme; the product is dark by design for night use.
